Services

Four ways I can help. Project or ongoing.

I take on analysis, engineering, BI and experimentation work, either as a single project or as an ongoing fractional role. See how engagements work.

Data analysis

Ad-hoc and ongoing analysis in SQL and Python. I take a business question, find the data that answers it, and explain the result in terms the people making the decision can use. That includes cleaning up inconsistent data and building reports you can rerun.

CASE STUDY · Modo Carshare

Data engineering and pipeline development

I design and build the infrastructure analytics depends on: ETL/ELT pipelines, data lakes and data warehouses, documented so your team can maintain them. My cloud work has been on AWS and GCP.

BI and dashboards

I help you choose a BI tool that fits your team and budget, then build the dashboards that make it useful. My tool experience includes Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio and custom Plotly-Dash apps.

CASE STUDIES · Modo Carshare · movmi mapping dashboard

Experimentation and A/B testing

I set up the analytics and experimentation foundation for product teams: event tracking, remote configuration and A/B tests, using Firebase.

CASE STUDY · Renown Entertainment

Industries

Transportation and video games, and beyond.

They're where I have the most direct experience, but the work (pipelines, warehouses, dashboards, experimentation) applies to any team with data that needs to be more reliable and useful.

If your industry isn't listed here, the work is the same: understand the question, get the data in order, and make it usable.

Transportation

Since 2020 I've done data work in shared mobility and carshare, through the consulting firm movmi and, since 2021, through Solid State Entity. Projects included a data warehouse and Power BI dashboards for Modo Carshare, and a mapping dashboard reused across many of movmi's clients.

Transportation data comes from vehicles, bookings, locations and operations, and it's often spread across systems that were never designed to work together. I know how to bring those sources together so operators can see what's happening across their fleet.

Modo Carshare · movmi mapping dashboard

Video games

I spent over ten years inside the game industry as a UI/UX designer and developer. I'm not claiming a decade as a game analyst. What that time gave me is a first-hand understanding of player behavior, game funnels, KPIs and monetization, so I know which questions are worth asking and what the numbers mean. Titles I've worked on include Metroid Prime: Federation Force (Nintendo 3DS), Tron: Evolution (Xbox 360, PS3, PC) and Hidden Agenda (Facebook).

On the analytics side, I integrated Firebase A/B testing across all released mobile games at Renown Entertainment.

Engagement models

Fractional or contract, sized to the work.

I work with clients as a fractional or contract data analyst and data engineer. There's no standard package: the size and length of an engagement depend on what you need.

Fractional

An ongoing, part-time role on your team. You get a data analyst or engineer for the hours you need without hiring someone full time. This suits teams with steady data work but not enough of it to fill a full-time position, or teams that want to build out data capability gradually.

Contract

Work with a defined scope or a set term, such as building a pipeline, designing a warehouse, delivering a set of dashboards, or running an analysis. This suits a specific need with a clear outcome.

Hours and duration

I don't have fixed hours or lengths. I'm open to whatever fits the work, from a short project to an ongoing arrangement.

Pricing

I bill hourly or on a retainer, depending on which suits the work. We'll agree on the structure and rate together once we've talked through what you need.

How I work

I work mostly remotely and can join occasional on-site sessions in the Vancouver area.

About

Data systems are another kind of interface.

I've always been fascinated by how people interact with technology: how an interface can open up something a person couldn't do on their own. That curiosity took me through more than a decade in the game industry as a UI/UX designer and developer, shipping titles on console, mobile and VR/AR, and eventually leading a team of nine as product owner.

Along the way I found that data systems are another kind of interface. A good pipeline, warehouse or dashboard gives a team clarity about what's happening and what to do next, the same way a good UI does for a player. That pulled me into data analysis and engineering, and since 2020 it's been the core of my work: building analytics for shared mobility operators and mobile game studios, in SQL, Python and the cloud.

Because I've worked on both sides, I can move between the technical work and the people who rely on it. I'm as comfortable writing the pipeline as explaining the result to someone who has never opened a query editor.

I'm a lifelong learner, and I'd rather learn a new tool for the job than force the old one to fit. My background is a BA in Cognitive Science from Simon Fraser University, a Data Engineering Nanodegree from Udacity (2020) and an AI Essentials Data Fellowship at SFU (2021).

Solid State Entity is the consulting practice I run. It's just me, so the person you talk to is the person who does the work.

If you have data that should be working harder for your team, I'd like to hear about it.
